Siapa yang pernah mendapat informasi bahwa vaksin campak menyebabkan kecacatan? Kabar itu hoaks ya, Moms!  Ketua Unit Kerja Koordinasi (UKK) Infeksi dan Penyakit Tropik Ikatan Dokter Anak Indonesia (IDAI) sekaligus Guru Besar Fakultas Ilmu Kedokteran Universitas Lambung Mangkurat, Prof. Dr. dr. Edi Hartoyo, Sp.A, Subs.IPT(K), menjelaskan vaksin campak tidak bisa menyebabkan rangsangan penyakit pada anak-anak yang diimunisasi.  Pada kesempatan yang sama, Ketua Satgas Imunisasi IDAI, Prof. DR. dr Hartono Gunardi, Sp.A, Subs.TKPS(K) membeberkan awal mula vaksin campak diisukan menyebabkan kecacatan dan autisme.  “Memang dulu, tahun 1990-an beredar (informasi) bahwa vaksin MMR, campak Jerman dan mumps gondongan, itu bisa menyebabkan anak autis. Jadi terlambat bicara, tidak bisa berinteraksi, ada gerak-gerak yang aneh atau stereotipik. Tapi itu penelitiannya hanya meliputi 12 anak yang diundang ke pesta ulang tahun peneliti tersebut,” ucap Prof. Hartono dalam acara webinar bersama IDAI, Rabu (27/8).  Prof. Hartono menegaskan penelitian tersebut tidak hanya cacat secara ilmiah, tetapi juga terbukti menyesatkan. Publikasi artikel tersebut telah ditarik, serta dokter yang mempublikasikannya dicabut izin praktiknya. Kabupaten Sumenep, Jawa Timur, kini berstatus kejadian luar biasa (KLB) penyakit campak. Menurut data Dinas Kesehatan Sumenep hingga Agustus 2025, terjadi 2.035 kasus campak dengan 17 kematian, dengan rincian 16 anak belum pernah diimunisasi dan satu anak tidak mendapat imunisasi lengkap.  Dikutip dari Antara, Gubernur Jawa Timur Khofifah Indar Parawansa sudah turun langsung untuk menangani KLB campak di Sumenep.  Untuk mencegah penyebaran lebih meluas, sebanyak 78.569 anak berusia 9 bulan hingga 6 tahun akan menjadi sasaran vaksinasi campak massal, yang berlangsung 25 Agustus-14 September 2025. Nantinya, akan ada pemberian satu dosis vaksin MR tanpa melihat status imunisasi sebelumnya.  “Secepatnya akan kami lakukan Outbreak Response Imunization atau ORI. Berdasarkan kajian epidemiologi sampai dengan 14 Agustus lalu, maka ORI campak akan dilakukan di 26 wilayah puskesmas di Sumenep untuk mencegah transmisinya,” kata Khofifah.  Setelah ORI dilakukan, akan ada imunisasi kejar pada anak-anak yang belum lengkap imunisasi campak sesuai usia. Sebelum membangun rumah tangga, ada satu langkah penting yang sering terlupakan: vaksinasi MMR! ⠀ MMR adalah vaksin kombinasi yang melindungi dari tiga penyakit berbahaya sekaligus: ✅ Measles (Campak) – penyakit menular yang bisa sebabkan komplikasi serius, termasuk radang paru hingga radang otak. ✅ Mumps (Gondongan) – bisa sebabkan pembengkakan kelenjar, nyeri hebat, bahkan gangguan kesuburan pada pria. ✅ Rubella – sangat berbahaya jika menyerang ibu hamil karena bisa menyebabkan kecacatan serius pada janin, seperti tuli, gangguan jantung, atau keterlambatan perkembangan.  🔎 Karena Rubella sering muncul tanpa gejala, seseorang bisa menularkan tanpa sadar—bahkan pada pasangan atau calon bayi. Inilah mengapa vaksin MMR sangat dianjurkan sebagai bagian dari premarital vaccine.  💉 Hanya dengan 1 suntikan, kamu bisa melindungi dirimu, pasangan, dan calon anak dari risiko kesehatan jangka panjang.  💍 Rencana nikah? Penyakit campak kembali menjadi ancaman serius di Eropa. Salah satu penyakit paling menular di dunia ini melonjak tajam sejak tahun lalu, dan tren tersebut belum menunjukkan tanda-tanda mereda di tahun 2025.  Menurut Pusat Pencegahan dan Pengendalian Penyakit Eropa (ECDC), sekitar 6.200 kasus campak telah dilaporkan di seluruh Uni Eropa hingga akhir Mei. Fenomena ini paling mencolok terlihat di kalangan anak-anak di bawah usia lima tahun yang belum divaksinasi. Padahal, meski campak sering kali hanya menimbulkan gejala ringan hingga sedang, komplikasi yang mematikan bisa saja terjadi.  Melansir Euronews, vaksin campak terbukti sangat efektif mencegah penularan namun sayangnya, tingkat vaksinasi di beberapa negara masih jauh dari target ideal.  Dengan 3.767 kasus dan tiga kematian yang tercatat hingga Mei 2025, Romania menjadi negara dengan jumlah kasus terbanyak di Uni Eropa. Wabah yang berlangsung bertahun-tahun ini diperparah oleh tingginya keraguan terhadap vaksin, panduan kesehatan yang bertentangan, serta sistem medis yang kesulitan mengimbangi situasi. Untuk itu, ambang batas antibodi dewasa saat ini digunakan untuk menentukan apakah anak-anak yang mengalami gangguan kekebalan tubuh harus mendapatkan suntikan penguat campak, gondongan, dan rubella (MMR).   Namun, sebuah studi baru menunjukkan bahwa ambang batas ini gagal mengidentifikasi persentase signifikan anak-anak yang perlu divaksinasi ulang.  Temuan yang dipublikasikan dalam Clinical Chemistry itu diyakini dapat membantu memastikan bahwa anak-anak yang mengalami gangguan kekebalan tubuh terlindungi dari virus-virus ini. Di tengah lonjakan kasus campak di berbagai belahan dunia, termasuk di Eropa dan Amerika Serikat, otoritas kesehatan AS kini mengubah arah kebijakan. Semua orang yang akan bepergian ke luar negeri wajib mendapatkan vaksin campak, tak peduli ke negara mana tujuannya.  Sebelumnya, Pusat Pengendalian dan Pencegahan Penyakit AS (CDC) hanya menganjurkan vaksin untuk mereka yang hendak pergi ke negara dengan wabah campak. Tapi sekarang, kebijakan itu diperluas untuk semua destinasi luar negeri.  Menurut Ashley Darcy-Mahoney, peneliti dari Sekolah Keperawatan Universitas George Washington, dunia kini menghadapi situasi baru dimana campak tak lagi hanya menyebar di satu negara, tapi juga di pesawat dan selama perjalanan.  Kasus terbaru di Colorado membuktikannya karena penyebaran dimulai dari satu penumpang dalam penerbangan internasional yang mendarat di Denver. Itu artinya, liburan ke negara yang dianggap "aman" sekalipun tetap membawa risiko.  “Kita sedang menyaksikan pergeseran dari wabah lokal ke penularan saat transit. CDC tampaknya mulai merespons hal itu,” ujar Darcy-Mahoney seperti dilansir dari Euronews. Mumps atau Gondongan disebabkan oleh virus yang disebut paramyxovirus A yang menginfeksi kelenjar liur terutama kelenjar parotis yang terletak di depan dan di bawah telinga. Virus ini juga dapat menginfeksi kelenjar ludah lainnya yang lebih rendah yang terletak di sepanjang rahang.  Penyakit ini dapat menimbulkan gejala sama seperti infeksi virus pada umumnya seperti demam, nyeri tenggorokan nyeri sendi dsb. Pemeriksaan antibodi atau pemeriksaan isolasi virus dapat membantu penegakan diagnosis mumps namun pemeriksaan ini tidak rutin dilakukan. Salt and Pepper, Anyone?  Congenital rubella  Today’s case was submitted by Fraser McKay (@fraser_mckay).  This 59YO male with type 2 diabetes was examined for his yearly screening. He has a known history for congenital rubella with deafness. Vision was 20/30 OD and 20/25 OS.  Optos color RGB imaging shows a diffuse salt and pepper appearance to each fundus with peripapillary atrophy (images 1 and 2). On fundus autofluorescence (FAF) the peripapillary atrophy is hypo-FAF with a speckled hyper- and hypo-FAF appearance to each posterior pole. Slit lamp photographs show diffuse iris atrophy with a relative lack of pigmentation. Triton swept-source OCT shows variable outer retinal thinning with ellipsoid zone disruption (images 3 and 4).  The classic ocular findings in congenital rubella include cataracts, pigmentary retinopathy ("salt-and-pepper" fundus), congenital glaucoma, and microphthalmia. Nuclear cataracts are the most common ocular abnormality, although our patient had just trace nuclear sclerosis. The pigmentary retinopathy is characterized by diffuse mottling of the retinal pigment epithelium which is best visualized with FAF. Systemic associations include sensorineural hearing loss and congenital heart defects.  Go to www.retinarocks.org/cases for more rubella cases. KARACHI: Sindh’s health minister launched 13-day vaccination drive against measles and rubella from Nov. 17 (today) till Nov. 29.  Measles and rubella are highly contagious diseases that continue to pose health challenges.  In the campaign children between the ages of 6 months to 5 years will be provided free MR vaccine in 30 districts of Sindh.  Moreover, polio drops will also be administered to children of up to five years in 23 districts of the province.  The province has deployed over 30,000 frontline staff including 6,532 vaccinators and equal number of team assistants for the vaccination drive.  Health Minister Azra Fazal Pechuho speaking on the occasion asked the vaccinators to perform their duty with serious commitment and complete their daily targes of the campaign.  “It is legally mandatory to vaccinate children, action will be taken in case of non-cooperation from parents or institutions,” minister said. “Licenses could be cancelled and institutions shutdown, if the private or government schools failed to cooperation”, Pechuho said.  She also directed for constitution of special teams to tackle the cases of resistance, which should report on daily basis.  “The National Cybercrime Agency will take action in case of spreading fake information or rumors about vaccination,” minister said.  “Those involved in negative propaganda or rumour mongering would pose threat to the health of children,” she added.  While all three diseases are preventable through vaccination, sporadic outbreaks in the past have highlight gaps in immunization coverage, misinformation and access to health care in remote areas.  In specific high-risk districts, polio drops will be administered along with measles, rubella vaccine so that every child is protected.  The measles-rubella (MR) vaccine will protect 35 million children aged 6 months to under five years nationwide, the NEOC said.  Measles and rubella spread through respiratory droplets and can cause pneumonia and encephalitis.  #arynews #measles #rubella #vaccination

Orang tua perlu sadar imunisasi itu bukan sekadar “opsional”, tapi benteng utama melindungi anak bre. Waktu pelaksanaan imunisasi vaksin Measles Rubella (MR) tinggal tiga bulan lagi, namun capaian di Kabupaten Jombang, Jawa Timur masih belum maksimal. Hingga awal Oktober, sebagian target imunisasi masih berada di bawah 50 persen.   Berdasarkan data Dinas Kesehatan, vaksin MR pertama ditargetkan menyasar 19.855 bayi usia 9 bulan. Hingga kini, 17.364 bayi sudah mendapat imunisasi atau setara 72 persen.   Untuk MR kedua yang menyasar 19.931 bayi usia 18 bulan, capaiannya baru 9.599 bayi atau 48 persen.   Sementara itu, MR ketiga bagi 19.032 siswa kelas 1 SD sudah mencapai 88 persen, dengan jumlah penerima 16.775 siswa.  Hexawan juga menjelaskan, vaksin MR sangat penting untuk meningkatkan kekebalan tubuh anak, khususnya balita yang rentan terhadap virus campak dan rubella.  “Vaksin MR dapat diberikan di pos imunisasi atau posyandu, juga di puskesmas, maupun sekolah untuk anak usia sekolah,” jelasnya.  Dinas Kesehatan mencatat hingga Mei 2025 ada dua anak terpapar campak dan dua anak terpapar rubella. Untuk mencegah penyebaran lebih luas, pihaknya melakukan sweeping dan imunisasi kejar.  Ke depannya harus diperbaiki biar tidak ada yang terpapar. A lot of people have genuine questions about routine vaccines. Between headlines, politics, and fear, it can be hard to find nuanced answers.  So we put this together to answer some of the biggest questions we hear: ✔️ Did sanitation and nutrition, not vaccines, really stop measles? ✔️ Why do we require vaccines for diseases that aren’t even endemic here anymore, like rubella? ✔️ Do the benefits of measles vaccination still outweigh the risks, given today’s low case counts? ✔️ Why does every U.S. baby get the hep B vaccine, even if their family seems “low risk”? ✔️ Why does the U.S. recommend universal vaccination when other countries target only certain groups?  Bottom line: vaccines are often victims of their own success. They’ve quietly prevented infections, disabilities, and deaths we no longer see. They remain one of the strongest public health protections we have.  We can’t reiterate this enough: Parents don’t need fear. If you are planning to have a baby, try to have your routine vaccinations up to date before you become pregnant.  Book an appointment to speak with your health professional. They may order a blood test to check your immunity to some diseases (including #rubella, #chickenpox and #hepatitis B) to see if you are protected. Based on the results, your health professional may recommend some #vaccines.  You can get the #influenza, #whoopingcough (#pertussis) and respiratory syncytial virus (#RSV) vaccines for free while you are pregnant through the National Immunisation Program (#NIP).  You can safely have the NIP influenza, whooping cough and maternal RSV vaccine in the same visit as recommended by your health professional.  COVID-19 vaccines can also be given at the same time as NIP maternal #vaccines if your health professional recommends it.  #ImmuniseForTwo #VaccinateInPregnancy #ProtectNewborns ##ImmuniseForTwo #VaccinateInPregnancy #ProtectNewborns ##vaccinesworkVaccinesWork

Fever, irritability, and rashes in children can signal a range of viral infections that require different key recognitions but mainly supportive care. Measles presents with a classic face/neck rash that spreads, accompanied by Koplik spots (red with white centres on buccal mucosa), URTI symptoms, and no cervical lymphadenopathy. Remember: measles = rubeola. — Rubella causes a low-grade fever and maculopapular rash starting on the face, fading by day 3–5, with characteristic cervical, suboccipital, and postauricular lymphadenopathy. Forscheimer’s spots (red petechiae on the soft palate) are important clues. — Roseola (exanthem subitum) begins with sudden high fever and is followed by a non-itchy rash on the chest or legs, later spreading across the body—commonly seen in infants and toddlers. — Erythema infectiosum (fifth disease) caused by parvovirus B19 gives a “slapped cheek” bright red rash, sometimes spreading and itchy, especially on the soles of the feet. — Hand, foot, and mouth disease due to Coxsackie virus leads to painful ulcers on the tongue and grey blisters on the hands and feet. The very first seed of doubt was planted when I was pregnant with my first baby. My OB told me I wasn’t immune to rubella. I was shocked because my mom never missed a booster shot when I was growing up. I thought vaccines were 100% safe and effective. I didn’t know immunity could “wear off.”  I trusted my OB and got a Tdap during pregnancy. Then after delivery—without my knowledge—I was given an MMR.  Fast forward to my second pregnancy, two years later. By then I had researched vaccines inside and out, and I had already decided to stop giving them to my son. My midwife told me I still wasn’t immune to rubella. I checked my hospital records from my son’s birth and sure enough, they had given me the MMR.  That was the moment I asked myself: what’s the point? If my body doesn’t respond, why would I keep getting another booster after every pregnancy?  Now here I am in my 6th pregnancy, and once again, I’m being told I’m not immune to rubella. After all these babies, you’d think they would stop bringing it up. 🙃  #vaccinestory #rubella #informedchoices #crunchymom #momcommunity #motherhoodjourney #healthfreedom #naturalwellness #holisticliving

Salam Sehat Sahabat Mas Barjo  Bulan Imunisasi Anak Sekolah (BIAS) untuk Campak dan Rubella telah dilaksanakan pada bulan Agustus. Program ini merupakan pemberian imunisasi lanjutan atau booster yang diberikan di sekolah, madrasah, dan pesantren untuk anak-anak usia sekolah dasar kelas 1 agar kekebalan tubuhnya terhadap campak dan rubella tetap kuat, terutama karena kekebalan dari imunisasi bayi dapat menurun seiring waktu.   Tujuan dan Manfaat BIAS Campak dan Rubella : - Meningkatkan Kekebalan: Memberikan kekebalan tubuh anak usia sekolah terhadap penyakit menular seperti campak dan rubella, yang dapat menyebabkan komplikasi serius.  - Mencegah Penyakit Menular: Melindungi anak-anak dari penyakit campak dan rubella yang dapat berdampak jangka panjang pada kesehatan mereka.  - Melengkapi Imunisasi Dasar: Memastikan anak mendapatkan perlindungan jangka panjang dengan melengkapi imunisasi yang telah diberikan saat bayi dan balita.    #bulanimunisasianaksekolah  #campak  #rubella

Lakukan surveilans imunisasi aktif pd kondisi wabah: detect, prevent, respond  Detect: diagnosis kasus campak klinis dan konfirmasi laboratorium darah sebanyak mungkin, isolasi segera di rumah / RS untuk memutus mata rantai penularan  Prevent: sweeping imunisasi anak, lengkapi segera, berikan imunisasi tambahan campak rubella di daerah wabah (ORI / outbreak response immunization)  Respond: tatalaksana segera selain diisolasi berikan obat2an seperti vitamin A utk cegah kebutaan, nutrisi yg baik, perbaikan kebersihan lingkungan dan sanitasi di rmh dan sekolah  Kenapa bisa wabah? Cakupan imunisasi tidak tinggi, merata, bermutu. Tinggi artinya cakupan imunisasi anak harus 95-100%. Ada 15 jenis imunisasi GRATIS dr pemerintah dr bayi baru lahir, balita, anak SD, wanita usia subur  Apa yg menyebabkan orang kena campak? Tidak vaksin campak sama sekali, tidak vaksin campak lengkap saat bayi, balita, SD, gizi kurang atau buruk, lingkungan sanitasi rumah tidak bersih, ventilasi udara dan cahaya buruk. The World Health Organization (WHO) recently announced that Nepal has eliminated rubella as a public health problem. Rubella, also called German measles or three-day measles, is a contagious viral infection known for its red rash. It is caused by the Rubella virus, a single-stranded RNA virus, different from the measles virus. Rubella spreads through coughing, sneezing, contaminated surfaces, and from mother to fetus during pregnancy. This can lead to fetal death or Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS), causing hearing loss, eye and heart defects, autism, diabetes mellitus, and thyroid problems. It was my niece’s 7th birthday when we met her. She tried her best to play along with Nisham, but he wanted to play alone. A little upset, she asked her grandmother (my Badi Mummy), “Why isn’t bhaiya playing?”  Badi Mummy lovingly tried explaining a few things, and somewhere in that conversation came the word “special.” It was a commendable effort on her part though.   A little later, my niece came to me and asked, “Why is bhaiya special?” At first, I was a little surprised-maybe even shocked-and I asked her how she learned that word. She then poured out all the questions running in her mind: "Bhaiya bachpan se hi chashma pehnta hai?" "Bhaiya kabhi baat nahi kiya?" and so on.  I replied patiently, and she listened carefully, trying her best to understand.  So, how should you respond in such scenarios? If your kids meet any special needs child and ask you this question, here are a few gentle ways to explain:  1. Keep it simple and relatable- Use the words like -Different and unique as everyone is special in their own ways.  "You know how everyone is different? Some people run fast, some love to draw, and some remember every detail of a story. Similarly Bhaiya is different and you are different."  2. Highlight strengths, not just differences "Bhaiya might take longer to talk or play games, but he’s amazing at remembering things, he loves hugs and he loves alphabets too."   3. Use kindness as the foundation "Being different doesn’t mean better or worse - it just means unique. And we treat everyone with the same kindness, no matter how they are."  4. Make it feel natural, not medical Avoid jargon or diagnoses. At that age, children understand feelings and abilities better than medical explanations.  5. Encourage curiosity with empathy If they ask more, say, "It’s okay to be curious, and it’s okay to ask. We just remember to speak with love." So, always greet everyone with a smile, be kind and try to make them comfortable.   #inclusive #inclusion #parentingspecialneeds #specialneedsparenting #autismmom  #autismacceptance #adhd #rubella

🧚🏻‍♀️TORCHES 🧚🏻‍♀️Powerful Prenatal blood test  Not every infection comes with a fever. Some come with lifelong consequences for your baby.  When you’re expecting a baby, it’s not just vitamins and scans that matter. Some silent infections can cross the placenta and affect your baby’s development.  That’s why doctors screen for a group of infections called:  🧬 TORCHES Antibodies  A powerful prenatal blood test — checking for infections that may harm a fetus.  🔍 What Does TORCHES Stand For?  T – Toxoplasmosis (Can come from undercooked meat or cat poop. May cause eye/brain issues in baby.)  O – Other: Includes syphilis, varicella, HIV, Zika, parvovirus B19  R – Rubella (German measles) (Can cause heart defects, deafness, or cataracts if mom is infected in early pregnancy.)  C – Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (Common virus that can cause hearing loss or learning delays in the newborn.)  H – Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) (Risk of brain inflammation or severe neonatal infection.)  E/S – Enteroviruses, Syphilis, or Expanded depending on lab panels  🤰 Why It Matters:  ✅ Protects your baby from hidden infections ✅ Helps your doctor take action before it’s too late ✅ Detects IgM (recent infection) and IgG (past exposure or immunity)  TORCHES screening isn’t just a test. According to German New Medicine (GNM), many skin conditions are linked to separation conflicts — moments when a person feels emotionally or physically separated from someone or something important. These conflicts can be experienced either as painful separations or as unwanted distances.  For example, herpes may appear after a “kiss-related” separation conflict — when someone wants to break up or quite the opposite: when they don’t want to part with their partner. The body reacts to this emotional pain by triggering a program in the skin near the mouth.  Urticaria (hives) often shows up during the healing phase of a separation conflict. If the person experienced fear or shock at the time of the conflict, the body may retain water (due to the kidney collecting tubules), leading to swelling, blisters, and intense itching.  Diseases like measles, rubella, and chickenpox also occur in the healing phase of widespread separation conflicts. These are common in children, as they are more vulnerable to feelings of separation from their “pack” — which could be their family, classmates, or caregivers.  Even psoriasis and vitiligo can reflect long-term or recurring separation conflicts, where the brain perceives a repeated emotional disconnection from a loved one or familiar environment.  All these conditions are not malfunctions, but meaningful biological programs with specific emotional roots.  #GermanNewMedicine #GNM #HealWithIrina #SkinHealing #SeparationConflict #MindBodyConnection #HerpesMeaning #Urticaria #Measles #Rubella #Chickenpox #Psoriasis #Vitiligo #PsychoEmotionalHealing

The wife of the Oyo Governor, Engr. Tamunominini Makinde, has led a sensitisation rallies on lifesaving vaccines on Measles, Rubella for children between age 9 months and 15 years.  The event which is an initiative of the Renewed Hope Initiative took place at Government Secretariat, Agodi, Ibadan.  It had in attendance wives of the lawmakers, members of the State Executive Council, caregivers, community leaders and healthcare service providers.  The sole aim of the programme is to boost awareness and uptake of vaccines to prevent measles and rubella, especially among children.  In her address, the First Lady appealed to the stakeholders to support government efforts to curb deaths from vaccine-preventable diseases, particularly among children aged five and below.  “As mothers and leaders in our communities, we must ensure every child receives the necessary vaccination to prevent avoidable deaths,” she said. She also charged the wives of chairmen from all 33 local government areas in the state to take the campaign door-to-door, ensuring no child is left behind.”  Earlier in her welcome address, the Oyo State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi, emphasized that measles remains one of the leading causes of child mortality globally. She also noted that rubella poses severe risks, particularly for pregnant women.  Rubella, according to her, can result in lifelong complications such as visual impairment, congenital blindness, deafness, and mental and growth retardation,  “These are not just personal tragedies but burdens on families and entire communities.”  She noted the challenges being faced to include, lack of awareness and cultural disbelief in vaccination among others.  She, therefore, reiterated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that no child dies from vaccine-preventable diseases.  “The vaccination campaign targets children aged 9 months to 15 years and includes integrated child health interventions such as vitamin A supplementation”.  #firstlady #measlesvaccine #rubella #oyodecides2027 #oyostategovernment #womeninpower #renewedhopeinitiative #vaccination #health #children #oyostate #rubellavaccination

Saat penderita ketiga penyakit tersebut batuk atau bersin, dahak atau percikan air liur yang keluar bisa saja terhirup oleh siapa pun yang ada didekatnya.  Jika hal ini terjadi, orang yang menghirup percikan dahak atau air liur bisa tertular. Inilah yang mendasari mengapa orang dewasa juga perlu mendapatkan vaksin MMR. You probably know there is an ongoing outbreak of measles in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, but did you know that there are several different diseases with “measles” in their everyday name? Rubeola is responsible for the large, ongoing outbreak that began in West Texas earlier in 2025. 😷  🦠 The disease “measles” is caused by a virus. A virus is a tiny particle stuffed with its own instruction booklet on how to make copies of itself. The instructions are written in either DNA or RNA language, depending which type of virus it is. Just like food recipes, the instructions for each virus are unique and equip the virus with different ways to infect the body and cause disease. Even if they’re different, many viruses can cause shared symptoms like rashes.   ❓What are these viruses? Let’s break it down in the slides.  💉The MMR vaccine was introduced in 1969. Once introduced, the number of measles and Rubella cases was reduced by over 99%. The CDC declared Rubeola disease eliminated in the US in 2000 and Rubella in 2004 due to the successful immunization campaign. This means that most cases happen in unvaccinated people who got the virus while they were outside of the US. Unfortunately, there is an ongoing outbreak of measles this year, leading to a large increase in cases.  ➡️ Bottom line, there are many different viruses that can cause a measles-like rash. Fortunately, Rubeola and Rubella are covered by the MMR vaccine. Since it can be hard to tell apart the rashes caused by viruses, it is always best to check with your trusted clinician if your child, or a family member, develops a rash. The best way to protect you and your family is to stay up to date on your vaccines. Hepatitis A is a viral infection. It spreads rapidly, causing fever, body aches, jaundice and stomach issues. There is no cure for hepatitis A, but it can be cleared by the body in about 2 months. It usually affects the liver but does not cause lasting damage. In rare cases, it can cause liver failure and death, but this is more common in individuals over 50 years of age or those with other conditions that affect the liver.  Vaccination against Hepatitis A is recommended if you are travelling to countries where there are poor levels of sanitation and hygiene, and Hepatitis A is common, this includes parts of Africa, Asia, and South America. Viral Rashes in Paediatrics – Classic Exam Patterns You Must Know! 	1.	Measles (Rubeola) → Face/neck first → spreads to body, Koplik spots on buccal mucosa, fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis. → No cervical lymphadenopathy. → Mnemonic “K” = Koplik, Cough, Coryza, Conjunctivitis. → Notifiable disease. Management: Support + Reassurance only. 	2.	Rubella (German Measles) → Similar rash but milder, with lymphadenopathy (cervical, suboccipital, postauricular). → Forscheimer’s spots on soft palate, not buccal mucosa. 	3.	Roseola (HHV-6) → Sudden high fever, then non-itchy rash on chest/legs → spreads to body. → Classic PLAB recall. 	4.	Parvovirus B19 (Fifth disease) → Slapped cheek rash, bright red cheeks → may spread to body. → Be cautious in pregnancy and SCD patients (aplastic crisis!). 	5.	Hand, Foot & Mouth (Coxsackie Virus) → Painful oral ulcers + grey vesicles on palms, soles. → Rash is non-pruritic. Supportive only. 🩺 German Measles (Rubella): A PA Student’s Guide to Exanthem #3 🌸  Rubella, also known as German measles, is a mild but highly contagious viral illness that poses serious risks in pregnancy. Recognizing this exanthem is crucial for preventing congenital complications! 🚨  💥 What is Rubella? Cause: Rubella virus (a Togavirus). Transmission: Respiratory droplets; incubation period 14-21 days. Key Concern: Congenital rubella syndrome (CRS) in pregnancy.  🔍 Classic Signs and Symptoms: Prodromal Phase (Often mild or absent in children) Low-grade fever, headache. Postauricular, occipital, and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy (classic finding!). Rubella Rash (Appears 1-5 days after prodrome) Pink, maculopapular rash that starts on the face and spreads downward. Spreads faster than measles and fades within 3 days ("3-day measles"). Forchheimer Spots (25% of cases) Small, red spots on the soft palate.  ⚡ Diagnosis: Clinical Diagnosis (based on symptoms and history). Confirmatory Tests: Rubella IgM antibodies (serology). PCR of nasopharyngeal swab.  ⚡ Management: Supportive Care (hydration, fever control). Isolation Precautions: Droplet precautions for 7 days after rash onset. Pregnancy Consideration: Congenital rubella syndrome (CRS) risk → requires IgG testing and counseling.  ⚡ Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS) Risks: Highest risk if infection occurs in the 1st trimester. Classic triad: Sensorineural deafness (most common). Cardiac defects (PDA, pulmonary artery stenosis). Cataracts or microphthalmia. Other complications: Hepatosplenomegaly, blueberry muffin rash, mental disability.  ⚡ Prevention: ✅ MMR Vaccine 2-dose schedule (1st dose at 12-15 months, 2nd dose at 4-6 years). Preconception Screening: Women of childbearing age should confirm immunity before pregnancy.  📚 Pro Tip: Think "Postauricular lymphadenopathy + descending rash = Rubella."  #PAStudent #FuturePA #Rubella #GermanMeasles #Exanthem #MMRVaccine #Pediatrics #PANCEPrep #MedicalEducation #PAJourney #LearnMedicine #InfectiousDisease #CongenitalRubella #PAGuide

Repost from @infantrisk • Measles is a virus which spreads easily from person to person, especially through coughs, sneezes, and even just being in the same room as someone who is sick. 🤧 The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after an infected person leaves. If someone is not immune, there’s a very high chance (up to 90%) they’ll get sick after being exposed.  Symptoms of measles usually start with a high fever, feeling very tired, and three main signs: cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes. 🌡 Tiny white spots may appear inside the mouth (called Koplik spots), and a rash soon follows—starting on the face and spreading down the body.  For babies and young children, measles can be especially dangerous. It can lead to pneumonia, swelling of the brain (encephalitis), and a weakened immune system which makes it easier to catch other illnesses for several years afterward.  Breastfeeding and the Measles Vaccine: If you’re a breastfeeding mom 🤱 and haven’t had your MMR vaccine (for measles, mumps, and rubella), it’s safe to get it—even while nursing. The vaccine does not harm your baby, and it may actually help.  While breastfeeding doesn’t directly protect your baby from catching measles, your body might pass some helpful antibodies through your milk after you get vaccinated. Researchers are currently studying this to see just how much protection breast milk might offer.  What About Vitamin A?: Vitamin A has been used in the treatment of measles in certain patients. However, it’s a fat-soluble vitamin, which means too much of it can build up in the body and cause toxicity. Vitamin A also transfers into breast milk, and large maternal doses during breastfeeding could pose risks to the infant.  📲 Visit infantrisk.com for greater details and access to research.  #InfantRiskCenter #BreastfeedingSupport #MommyMeds #infantriskhcp #ibclc #breastfeeding #breastmilk #MMR #MMRvaccine #measels #mumps #rubella #measlesmumpsrubella

😷 Votre famille est-elle protégée contre la rougeole? Il y a une éclosion en cours au Québec, et c’est maintenant qu’il faut agir.  Depuis décembre, 40 cas ont été confirmés dans la province. Pour l’instant, la ville de Québec n’a pas de cas déclarés, mais la rougeole est très contagieuse — un seul cas peut tout changer.  MAIS CE N’EST QU’UN VIRUS, LE CORPS NE PEUT-IL PAS LE COMBATTRE SEUL ?  C’est une question fréquente et logique. Mais certains virus, même s’ils semblent bénins, peuvent causer de graves dommages.  Pensez au VIH, à la rage, à la COVID 🤔🤔🤔  La rougeole peut également être dangereuse. La différence, c’est que le vaccin a presque éradiqué le virus. C’est pourquoi on l’oublie. Mais le risque est toujours là. Et quand la vaccination diminue, le virus en profite.  Rappelez-vous : la prévention est ce qui rend les problèmes lointains.  QUI SONT LES PLUS VULNÉRABLES ?  📌 Bébés de moins d’un an  📌 Femmes enceintes  📌 Personnes immunodéprimées   Et surtout : ces personnes ne peuvent pas être vaccinées. C’est donc à nous de les protéger.  LES COMPLICATIONS DE LA ROUGEOLE PEUVENT ÊTRE GRAVES  📌 Surdité ou cécité  📌 Lésions neurologiques irréversibles  📌 Et même la mort (1 cas sur 3 000)  Il n’existe aucun traitement pour éliminer le virus. On peut seulement soutenir le corps pendant qu’il lutte.  CONTAGION ET SYMPTÔMES : quelques minutes dans le même espace suffisent. Et les symptômes ressemblent à ceux d’une grippe 👇👇👇  - Fièvre  - Nez qui coule  - Yeux rouges  - Sensibilité à la lumière  - Malaise général  Vérifier votre carnet de vaccination peut protéger ceux que vous aimez — et même ceux que vous ne connaissez pas, mais qui dépendent de vous. Parlez-en à un professionnel de santé et gardez votre famille protégée. 3D structures that mimic the human brain   Organoids are miniaturized versions of organs, grown in a Petri dish. While not exact replicas of human organs, they offer significant insights and provide platforms for disease modeling, drug testing, and understanding developmental processes.  The Siegert group at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) now presents a new brain organoid model that reveals details of the developing nervous system’s response to viral infections, such as Rubella.   For the first time, their model integrates microglia—special cells that scan our brain for germs and initiate an anti-inflammatory response to remove them—to mimic inflammatory reactions and their treatment.  Published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation, this model could influence pharmaceutical testing, particularly benefiting drug safety for pregnant women. 🚨 Rubella: Protect Yourself & Your Baby! 🚨  Rubella is a contagious virus that spreads through coughing and sneezing. While postnatal rubella is usually mild, it can cause severe birth defects if contracted during pregnancy.  💥 Symptoms (Develop 14-23 days after exposure & last ~3 days): ✅ Mild fever & headache ✅ Pink or red rash (starts on the face, spreads to the body) ✅ Swollen lymph nodes ✅ Joint pain (especially in teens & adults)  ⚠️ Serious Risks for Pregnant Women ⚠️ If a woman gets rubella during pregnancy, the baby can develop Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS), leading to: ❌ Deafness ❌ Blindness (cataracts) ❌ Heart defects ❌ Intellectual disabilities ❌ Growth retardation ❌ Liver & spleen enlargement ❌ Bleeding problems  Risk of birth defects: 🩸 85% if infected in the first trimester 🩸 54% between 13-16 weeks 🩸 25% by the end of the second trimester  🚫 No Treatment—Only Prevention! 🚫 The MMR vaccine (measles, mumps, rubella) 💉 is the best protection against rubella and its devastating effects on unborn babies.  Before the vaccine, rubella outbreaks led to thousands of birth defects. What is the Measles Virus?  The measles virus (MeV) is a negative-sense, single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Paramyxoviridae family. It possesses a lipid envelope with two surface proteins, hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) and fusion protein (F). MeV uses its HN protein to initiate infection by binding to specific receptors on the host cell's surface, typically CD46, CD150 (SLAM), or nectin-4, depending on the type of host cell. Hence, the HN protein is the primary target of neutralizing antibodies (nAbs). The measles vaccine induces nAbs that target the HN protein and, to a lesser extent, also the F protein. #measles #measlesoutbreak #mmrvaccine #mumps #rubella #masern #masernmumpsröteln #vaccines #vaccinessavelives #harvard #brown #dartmouth #upenn #columbia #yale #stanford #ucsd #ucberkeley #ucla #heidelberg #karolinska #impfungen #impfung #children #kinder #science #immunology #tcell #bcell #antigenpresentingcells

The news about the measles outbreak in Texas and New Mexico may have adults wondering, “Do I need a measles booster?” In most cases, the answer is no. Adults who have received at least one dose of the MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella) vaccine in their lifetime or have natural immunity from a previous infection are considered sufficiently protected.   Starting in 1989, @cdcgov recommended that all children receive two doses of the MMR vaccine – one dose at 12-15 months and the second dose between the ages of 4 and 6. Two doses of the measles vaccine provide lifetime protection and are 97% effective at preventing measles.   Adults born in 1957 or later should get at least one dose of the MMR vaccine unless they have proof of vaccination or immunity. Those born before 1957 are generally considered immune, except for healthcare workers, who need documented immunity. If you don’t know whether you had #measles as a child or received an MMR vaccine, talk to your healthcare provider or our immunization nurses to determine if vaccination is right for you.   Others who may want to consider getting a MMR booster if immunity is unknown:  🔸 People visiting an area where there is an ongoing measles outbreak or who travel internationally 🔸 College or trade school students 🔸 Healthcare workers 🔸 Close contacts of immunocompromised people   If you fall into one of these categories, discuss it with your healthcare provider and check your health benefit plan to determine if the MMR vaccine is covered. Parents are being urged to check for symptoms of measles and ensure their children's vaccinations are up to date.  Data published by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) shows Bristol has had the highest number of measles cases in the country this year.  With 25 cases, it has reached almost half the number reported in 2024. Dr Toyin Ejidokun at UKHSA South West said: "Measles is highly infectious, and it can cause serious disease or even death in some rare cases."  Dr Ejidokun said symptoms to look out for include cold-like symptoms, sore red eyes, a high temperature or a red-brown blotchy rash.  "If you experience these symptoms, seek medical attention, but please ensure that you phone ahead before visiting a healthcare setting, so that arrangements can be made to prevent others from being infected," he added. Julie Northcott, deputy director of public health at Bristol City Council, said measles spreads "very easily and quickly" among unvaccinated people.  "One person infected by measles can infect nine out of 10 of their unvaccinated close contacts," she said. "The MMR vaccine is safe and by far the most effective way to protect yourself and those around you." Approximately 14.9% of five-year-olds in Bristol have not had the MMR vaccination. 🔬 Different types of vaccines protect in different ways, making some more suitable for certain diseases, populations of people, and geographic regions.  🔹 Live-Attenuated vaccines use weakened germs to provide strong, long-lasting immune response. These require refrigeration, limiting use in some areas. Examples include #measles, #mumps, #rubella, #rotavirus, #YellowFever, and #chickenpox vaccines.  🔹 Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines use synthetic mRNA to make proteins that trigger an immune response. These are faster to manufacture and carry no risk of causing the disease because they do not contain a live virus. Examples include #COVID19 and #RSV vaccines.  🔹 Subunit, Recombinant, Polysaccharide, and Conjugate vaccines use specific parts of a pathogen, such as a carbohydrate, to produce a targeted immune response. Zwykle jej przebieg jest łagodny – z wysypką, gorączką i osłabieniem. Jednak dla kobiet w ciąży, szczególnie w pierwszym trymestrze, może stanowić poważne zagrożenie dla rozwijającego się dziecka.  🌹 Zakażenie różyczką w pierwszych 16 tygodniach ciąży może prowadzić do tzw. zespołu różyczki wrodzonej (CRS – congenital rubella syndrome). Zespół różyczki wrodzonej (CRS) przebiega z zaćmą, utratą słuchu, wadami serca i zaburzeniami ze strony ośrodkowego układu nerwowego.  🌹 Im wcześniej dojdzie do zakażenia, tym większe ryzyko poważnych powikłań dla dziecka.  🌹 Największe ryzyko wystąpienia CRS występuje w krajach, w których kobiety w wieku rozrodczym nie mają odporności na tę chorobę - ani w wyniku szczepienia, ani w wyniku przebytej różyczki.  🌹 Najlepszym sposobem ochrony jest szczepienie przeciw różyczce. Kobiety planujące ciążę, które nie mają odporności (nie były szczepione lub nie przechodziły różyczki), powinny zaszczepić się co najmniej 3 miesiące przed poczęciem. W ciąży szczepienie jest przeciwwskazane, dlatego ważna jest wcześniejsza profilaktyka!  🌹 Jak można zapobiec zakażeniu różyczką w ciąży? Prelicensure clinical trials for vaccines, including the MMR shot, are “relatively small and usually last no longer than a few years,” according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) 2024 “Manual for the Surveillance of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases.”  Dr. Shira Miller explained that the MMR vaccine clinical trials didn’t include enough subjects to be able to prove that the risk of permanent disability or death from the vaccine is less than the risk of permanent disability or death from measles, mumps or rubella.  No safety studies on the MMR vaccine have been done that looked for possible genetic mutations, impaired fertility or cancer, according to the product’s package insert.  Also, seizures from the MMR vaccine occur five times more often than measles-related seizures. On January 30, during his nomination hearing, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was asked about a claim he made in 2021. The claim was that “We should not be giving Black people the same vaccine schedule that’s given to whites, because their immune system is better than ours” (1,2). But is this true?   Not according to the very same study he was referencing. A 2014 study on immune responses to the rubella vaccine based on race, sex, and genetics found that, on average, individuals of African descent had higher neutralizing antibody levels after rubella vaccination compared to individuals of European descent or Hispanic ethnicity (3). But what does this actually mean? 👇  First, this is a hypothesis-generating study, which explores patterns and relationships to guide future research – it doesn’t establish cause-and-effect. Larger confirmatory studies are needed to rigorously test these hypotheses before drawing conclusions. Treating findings from hypothesis-generating studies as definitive is misleading (2,4,5).   Secondly, the study never looked into whether the difference resulted in better protection against infection or if the higher antibody levels were even due to vaccination. The study also never suggested changing current vaccine recommendations according to race (2,3).   All this paper does is further highlight the natural variability in immune responses, which have been observed with other vaccines – at times being stronger in one population and at other times in another (3,6-11).   Beyond being misleading, claims like this are harmful. Equity-deserving communities already face barriers to healthcare, and remain under-vaccinated (12-16). Large-scale studies have repeatedly shown the benefits of routine vaccination (17-24), yet misinformation like this risks widening existing health disparities. Campak adalah infeksi virus yang sangat menular dan sering kali dimulai seperti flu biasa. Setelah masa inkubasi sekitar 10–14 hari, anak mulai menunjukkan demam tinggi, batuk-pilek, dan mata merah. Banyak orang tua tidak menyadari bahwa pada tahap ini anak sudah bisa menularkan virus ke orang lain melalui batuk, bersin, atau udara yang terkontaminasi. Ruam khas campak biasanya muncul beberapa hari kemudian, bermula dari wajah dan cepat menyebar ke seluruh tubuh, sering disertai bercak putih kecil di dalam pipi (Koplik spots).  Di balik tampilannya yang terlihat seperti ruam biasa, campak memiliki potensi komplikasi berat. Pneumonia, diare berat yang menyebabkan dehidrasi, kejang, hingga infeksi otak adalah risiko nyata yang dapat terjadi, terutama pada bayi, anak dengan gizi kurang, atau mereka yang belum diimunisasi. Karena itu, campak bukan penyakit yang bisa ditunggu-tunggu atau dianggap ringan. Vaksinasi MR/MMR lengkap tetap menjadi perlindungan terbaik untuk mencegah penularan dan menurunkan tingkat keparahan penyakit. Bila anak mengalami ruam disertai demam tinggi, batuk-pilek, atau tampak sangat lemas, pemeriksaan segera sangat dianjurkan untuk mencegah terlambatnya penanganan.  #SehatBarengDrDewi #campak #ruamanak #measlesawareness #imunisasilengkap #vaksinMR #pediatrimedan #dokteranakmedan #demammanak #batukpilekanak #kesehatananak #edukasikesehatan #parentingmedan #pencegahancampak #wajibvaksin #RSIAStellaMaris #RSReginaMaris

Tenang Bunn, sini mimin jelasin sedikit apa itu KIPI ya,  KIPI adalah Kejadian Ikutan Pasca Imunisasi yang merupakan reaksi tubuh yang tidak diinginkan yang muncul pasca vaksinasi.  Nah, efek samping vaksinasi ini memiliki reaksi yang berbeda-beda di setiap orang, tergantung respons masing-masing anak, dan KIPI ini sendiri dibagi dalam 2 kelompok yakni KIPI ringan (lebih sering terjadi) seperti demam, bengkak, serta muncul ruam dan KIPI berat (sangat jarang terjadi). 🌱Dosis imunisasi BCG adalah 0,05 ml untuk bayi di bawah usia satu tahun. Umumnya penyuntikan imunisasi BCG dilakukan pada lengan bagian atas. Lengan bagian tersebut tidak boleh diberikan imunisasi lain, minimal selama 3 bulan.  🌱Meski tergolong imunisasi wajib, ada beberapa kondisi bayi yang membuat pemberian imunisasi BCG perlu ditunda, seperti demam,  infeksi kulit, dan bayi dari ibu dengan TB aktif. Bayi dari ibu yang menderita TB aktif perlu diberikan terapi pencegahan. Selain itu, imunisasi BCG tidak boleh diberikan pada bayi dengan HIV.  🌱Imunisasi BCG merupakan tindakan yang penting untuk melindungi kesehatan anak dari penyakit tuberkulosis. Namun, pastikan bayi dalam keadaan sehat sebelum mendapatkan vaksin BCG, ya.  🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃 Silahkan yang mau reservasi  Jl. SMA 14 cawang Kramat jati.
